text: Continuous integration (CI) is a practice where developers regularly add their code to a shared project. Every time someone makes a change, automated builds start immediately. These builds compile the code and check that everything works together. During the build, the system also runs tests to confirm the new code doesn't break anything. This helps teams catch issues early, before they become serious problems. A CI pipeline organizes all these steps into one clear process. When the pipeline succeeds, the team knows the code is safe to use. This saves time and makes software development smoother and more reliable.
